title: Performance specs assert on absolute wall-clock time (intermittency risk)
evidence: acceptance/specs/provided-datasets.spec.ts:128-134 assert simple lookups <2s and aggregates <5s, timed in acceptance/drivers/mcp-soccer-driver.ts:348-355 against elapsed wall-clock
suggestion: Move latency budgets out of the pass/fail acceptance suite into a separate perf check on a controlled host, or assert correctness here and only warn on timing, so an overloaded runner never reports the software as broken

title: Data-coverage spec hard-codes per-file record counts
suggestion: Acceptable as a coverage canary, but it is the most implementation-aware spec and will break on any data refresh; keep this pattern out of behavioural specs

title: A few specs name the dataset a match was 'recorded in'
suggestion: Forgivable because cross-dataset provenance is the behaviour under test; keep recordedIn naming a domain source, never a file name, as the suite grows

title: No CI wiring to gate releases on the suite
evidence: No .github/workflows (or equivalent) present in the run workspace
suggestion: Wire test:unit and test:acceptance into CI as distinct release-gating stages so the honest, trustworthy suite actually gates releasability

title: Implementation exceeds spec with 16 tools (derbies, knockout brackets, season comparison, team profile)
evidence: src/tools.ts registers find_matches, head_to_head, team_record, team_competitions, team_rankings, team_profile, standings, knockout_bracket, derbies, match_statistics, biggest_wins, compare_seasons, search_players, player_profile, players_by_club, dataset_overview
suggestion: No action; surfaced as positive coverage beyond the required capabilities
